## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Valāhakassajātaka* (Ja 196) is a narrative in the Pāli Jātaka collection told by the Buddha at Jetavana concerning a backsliding monk [SuttaCentral]. In the story, five hundred merchants are shipwrecked on an island (identified as Ceylon) inhabited by ogresses (*yakkhinī* or *rakkhasī*) who reside in the city of Sirisavatthu [Sutherland 1991; Anandajoti 2010]. These enchantresses seduce the shipwrecked sailors, marry them, bind them with magic chains, and imprison them in houses of torment to devour them [Sutherland 1991]. The Bodhisatta, appearing as a miraculous flying cloud-horse (*Ājāneyabalaha*), offers to rescue them and carry them across the ocean; while half of the merchants heed his warning and escape to safety, the other half remain behind and perish [Anālayo 2012; Anandajoti 2010; Sutherland 1991]. In the narrative's resolution, the Buddha identifies the flying horse with himself in a former existence [Anālayo 2012; Winternitz 1933].
Scholars have noted that the motif of the siren island and the rescue by the miraculous horse Balaha appears widely across Buddhist literature, including Sanskrit and Tibetan traditions, where it develops into the *Siṁhala-avadāna* found in the *Divyāvadāna* (as the *Rākṣasī-sūtra*), the *Mūlasarvāstivāda-vinaya*, and the *Kāraṇḍavyūha* [Thomas 1933; Winternitz 1933; Neelis 2011]. In these later versions, the Bodhisatta is often identified with the merchant leader Siṁhala, while the miraculous horse is identified as an emanation of Avalokiteśvara [Thomas 1933; Winternitz 1933; Dudjom Rinpoche 1991].
According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels to the verse are found in Sanskrit and Chinese collections of the Udānavarga, specifically in the *Tathāgatavarga* (UV 21, UVS 21, Uv Kg 21, and T 213.21) [SuttaCentral]. Machine text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identified no significant Pāli-internal or cross-language matches above threshold [DharmaNexus].

- Passage-level parallels (SuttaCentral): UV 21 Tathāgatavarga; T 213.21 法集要頌經如來品第二十一; Uv Kg 21 Tathāgatha; UVS 21 Tathāgatavarga
